name: IPv4 traffic
notes: Show IPv4 packets; does not include IPv6

name: VLAN-tagged
notes: 802.1Q when tags are present in capture

name: DHCPv4
notes: Modern Wireshark field for DHCPv4; legacy bootp appears in older versions

name: HTTP
notes: Only traffic dissected as HTTP; usually plaintext or decrypted

name: SMB2
notes: SMB2 and SMB3 messages decoded as SMB2

name: Either endpoint IPv4
notes: Use an actual address from the authorized network

name: Exclude IPv4 host
notes: IPv6/non-IP packets are not necessarily excluded

name: IPv4 subnet
notes: Either endpoint is within a private IPv4 range

name: Traffic leaving private range
notes: Not necessarily public internet; routed/private/VPN destinations exist

name: TCP port 443
notes: TCP only; excludes QUIC over UDP

name: UDP port 53
notes: DNS may also use TCP; DoH/DoT use others

name: DNS traditional transport
notes: Port match; does not guarantee DNS

name: TCP port range
notes: Either endpoint port in inclusive range

name: TCP stream 0
notes: Example index assigned by current capture

name: UDP stream 0
notes: Example index assigned by current capture

name: Frames over 1400 bytes
notes: Size only; not an indicator of exfiltration

name: Retransmission
notes: Analysis flag affected by trace completeness

name: Lost segment reported
notes: Wireshark analysis heuristic; not confirmed packet loss

name: Zero window
notes: Receiver advertises inability to accept data

name: Window full
notes: Receiver window may be limiting throughput

name: Zero window probe
notes: Sender checks whether peer window reopened

name: High observed ACK RTT
notes: 200 ms measured in current capture; perspective dependent

name: TCP relative time gap
notes: Greater than 1 second between TCP packets on a flow

name: DNS NXDOMAIN
notes: Name does not exist; common benign reasons

name: DNS name contains example
notes: Case/label semantics depend on dissected name

name: Long DNS question name
notes: Triage heuristic; legitimate domains can be long

name: DNS on unexpected port
notes: Decoder must recognize it; DoH generally not visible as dns

name: ARP replies
notes: All replies; not proof of ARP poisoning

name: Router advertisements
notes: Neighbor discovery RA; verify authorized router

name: TLS ClientHello
notes: TLS handshake from client; SNI not always visible

name: TLS alerts
notes: TLS alert record; may be encrypted

name: TLS SNI contains example
notes: SNI may be hidden by ECH or unavailable

name: HTTP POST
notes: POST is normal; not by itself suspicious

name: QUIC/HTTP3 transport candidate
notes: Many QUIC flows use UDP 443; not exclusive to QUIC

name: SMB TCP 445
notes: Port heuristic, independent of protocol decoding

name: RDP port 3389
notes: Port only; not an indicator of unauthorized access

name: SSH TCP 22
notes: SSH control traffic and data when visible

name: Possible SYN reconnaissance
notes: Only candidate pattern; validate rate/host context

name: Low TTL IPv4
notes: Common in routing diagnostics; not an intrusion proof

name: ICMP echo requests
notes: Potential ping/health checks; not a flood by itself

name: HTTP off common port
notes: Can be normal, e.g. proxies and admin apps

name: Non-initial IPv4 fragments
notes: May be intentionally fragmented or standard

name: TCP SYN destined to SSH
notes: Investigate bursts by source; no payload/credential insight

name: Disassociation
notes: Context and PMF are required for interpretation

name: Deauthentication
notes: Not proof of spoofing or successful disconnect

name: Deauth and disassoc
notes: For packet counts on a fixed channel with known capture gaps

name: 802.11 source address
notes: Reported source address; not guaranteed origin

name: Protected flag
notes: Do not treat alone as evidence of negotiated PMF

name: EAPOL handshake frames
notes: Not proof of authentication success or captured credentials

name: Exclude ARP
notes: Do not hide ARP while investigating spoofing

name: Exclude local discovery
notes: Use only after collecting full PCAP

name: Only DNS and TLS
notes: May miss encrypted DNS and QUIC
